chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'dan, from Hatim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I viewed that the act of kindness (al-ma'ruf) is not correct except with three characteristics: making it insignificant, concealing it, and hastening to it. For indeed, when you make it insignificant, you magnify it in the presence of the one to whom you are doing it; and when you conceal it, you complete it; and when you hasten to it, you make it welcoming; and if it were otherwise, you would trivialize it and cause annoyance.
ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that make an act of kindness perfect according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that for kindness (al-ma'ruf) to be spiritually complete, it must be minimized in the giver's eyes, concealed from public view, and executed promptly to avoid burdening the recipient. This triad of humility, modesty, and speed ensures the act remains a pure gift rather than a source of pride or obligation, a principle deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on social conduct.
